correctness.rationale: Exact edge-increment coordinate expansion and column norm; elementary telescoping gives the formula for all N, including boundaries \(N=2\) and rooted paths. Branching proves iff nonexpansivity. The log-integral upper bound and explicit construction with \(O(\sqrt N)\) cost yield sharp \(N/e\). The standalone program independently reproduces 8,726 exact tree cases, 250 larger tests, and four growing constructions. Finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: Descendant averaging is a natural hierarchical smoothing map, and variation is the natural edge cost for signals on trees. The complete path-only contraction classification is structurally informative; despite positivity, the worst variation norm grows linearly with graph size with exact coefficient \(1/e\). Explicit extremizing subtrees and near-extremal branched spines identify how amplification arises. The claim is not just a routine \(\ell^p\) matrix estimate or arbitrary finite-case table.
